{{MedalGold|[[Basketball at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2019 Lima]]|}} }} '''Gabriel Alejandro "Gaby" Deck''' (born February 8, 1995) is an Argentine professional [[basketball]] player for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. At a height of {{convert|1.98|m|ftin|abbr=on}}[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=009005 DECK, GABRIEL HEIGHT: 1.99.] he can play at both the [[small forward]] and [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] positions. ==Early career== In August 2011, Deck attended the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp held in [[Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]]. He was named the camp's [[most valuable player]].[http://bwb.fiba.com/camps/2011/rio-de-janeiro "BWB Americas 2011."] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140918131620/http://bwb.fiba.com/camps/2011/rio-de-janeiro |date=September 18, 2014 }}, ''[[FIBA]]''. Retrieved on 4 May 2015. He later played at the [[Nike Hoops Summit]] in 2013. ==Professional career== === Quimsa (2010–2016) === Deck started his professional career with the [[Liga Nacional de Básquet|Argentinian LNB]] club [[Quimsa]]. ===San Lorenzo (2016–2018)=== In 2016, Deck joined the Argentine club [[San Lorenzo de Almagro (basketball)|San Lorenzo]]. With San Lorenzo, he won the [[2018 FIBA Americas League]] championship while also being named the league's [[FIBA Americas League Awards|Grand Final MVP]]. Deck was also the competition's top scorer, with a scoring average of 19.1 points per game, over eight games played. ===Real Madrid (2018–2021)=== On July 19, 2018, Deck signed a three-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and [[EuroLeague]] after he reached a buyout agreement with [[San Lorenzo de Almagro (basketball)|San Lorenzo]].{{cite news |title=Deck joins Real Madrid {{!}} Real Madrid CF |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/07/deck-joins-real-madrid |access-date=19 July 2018 |work=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial |date=19 July 2018}}{{cite news |title=Official Announcement: Gabriel Deck {{!}} Real Madrid CF |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2018/07/official-announcement-gabriel-deck |access-date=19 July 2018 |work=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial |date=19 July 2018}} In his first season with the club, he made a debut in the [[2018–19 EuroLeague]] season, averaging 4.4 points and 2.4 rebounds over 31 games. He averaged 4.8 points and 2.9 rebounds in the Spanish League over 30 games. In his last season, Deck appeared in 58 games, averaging 9.7 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in 23.9 minutes while shooting 52.1 percent from the field.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Gabriel Deck to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/deck-210412|date=12 April 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=12 April 2021}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2021–2022)=== On April 12, 2021, Deck signed a multi-year contract with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. On April 29, Deck made his debut against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], scoring two points, grabbing two rebounds and dishing out two assists across 15 minutes in the Thunder's 109–95 loss.{{Cite web|title=Thunder's Gabriel Deck: Does little in debut|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/thunders-gabriel-deck-does-little-in-debut/|access-date=2021-05-02|website=CBSSports.com|date=30 April 2021 |language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Parker|first=Derek|title=Oklahoma City's Gabriel Deck flashes potential in NBA debut|url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/oklahoma-citys-gabriel-deck-flashes-potential-in-nba-debut|access-date=2021-05-02|website=Sports Illustrated|date=30 April 2021 |language=en}} On January 4, 2022, Deck was waived by the Thunder.{{Cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Miye Oni|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-oni-220104|access-date=January 4, 2022|website=Oklahoma City Thunder}} ===Return to Real Madrid (2022–present)=== On January 19, 2022, Deck returned to Real Madrid, signing a two-year deal.{{cite news |title=Official Announcement: Deck {{!}} Real Madrid CF |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/01/19/official-announcement-deck |access-date=16 February 2023 |work=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial |date=19 January 2022}} On June 28, 2023, Deck renewed his contract with the historic club through 2028. ==National team career== ===Junior national team=== With the junior national team of Argentina, Deck was the top scorer of the [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2012 FIBA Under-17 World Cup]], with an average of 21.5 points per game. He was selected to the [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. He also played at the [[2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2013 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]. ===Senior national team=== Deck also represented the senior men's [[Argentine national basketball team]] at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Championship|2015 FIBA AmeriCup]], in [[Mexico City]], where he won a silver medal. He recorded his team's best two-point field goal percentage during the tournament.[http://www.americas2015.com/en/jugador.asp?r=79872&c=ARG&n=Argentina&team=237 2015 FIBA Americas Championship – Gabriel Deck's profile], FIBA.com, accessed 11 Feb 2016. He also played at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]] and at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]]. In 2019, he participated in the team that won the [[Basketball at the 2019 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|Pan American gold medal in Lima]]. In 2022, Deck won the gold medal in the [[2022 FIBA AmeriCup]] held in [[Recife]], [[Brazil]]. He was Argentina's starting [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] in the tournament. After the final game against Brazil, he was named in the [[FIBA AmeriCup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]] and declared the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of the championship.{{cite
